idea: 055 Slow trend: follow 50-day breakouts on a basket of markets
hypothesis: A daily close at the highest (lowest) of the last 50 daily closes is followed over the next weeks by further moves in the same direction, on a basket of 14 FX, metal and index markets, enough to beat costs and the same-side random-day null.
mechanism: Time-series momentum (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012) and the long record of trend-following futures funds: slow diffusion of information, hedging and risk-parity flows that chase trends, central-bank paths that move currencies for months. Never tested by this lab because of the five-day hold cap (slow track now allows 40 trading days). Not a closed family: the closed breakout tests were intraday or held <= 5 days.

data.signal: prices only: kit.data.load_bars(key) prepared hourly BID bars (~/explore_data/h1). Daily close = close of the last hourly bar of the 17:00-New-York trading day (kit.data.trading_day), days with >= 5 hourly bars only (drops the one-bar holiday stubs); KNOWN at that trading day's 17:00 New York boundary (DST-correct), never earlier, even when the market closed earlier that day.
data.publication_lag: none (no external series). Each daily close is used from the 17:00 New York boundary of its day.
data.prices: kit.data.load_bars(<fp key>) = prepared hourly BID bars 2013-2021 (us30 and ger40 start 2013-09-30); FP costs from lab/r2/fp_costs.json (no provisional market).
data.in_sample_years: 2013 .. 2021 (9 years; us30 and ger40 8.25). Power check (signal data alone, no return): 5,080 breakout closes; 654 regime entries (a lower bound of the one-position trades, before stops and time exits add re-entries), 43-51 per market.

rule_main.signal: At each daily close c_t (known at the day's 17:00 NY boundary): long if c_t >= max(c_{t-49..t}) (the highest of the last 50 daily closes, itself included); short if c_t <= min(c_{t-49..t}). 50 complete days needed.
rule_main.side: +1 for the 50-day-high close, -1 for the 50-day-low close
rule_main.entry: open of the first hourly bar opening at or after the 17:00 NY boundary (kit.sim, delay 0, no max_wait)
rule_main.exit: exit on a condition (kit.sim.event_exit): long leaves at the open of the first bar at or after the boundary of a daily close that is the lowest of the last 20 closes (itself included), short at a close that is the highest of the last 20; or max hold 40 business days ('bdays', 40), whichever first. Events per market = the 20-day-low closes met while the market's breakout state is long and the 20-day-high closes met while it is short (state long from a 50-day-high close until the first 20-day-low close, short from a 50-day-low close until the first 20-day-high close): for every long trade the first event after its entry is exactly its first 20-day-low close, and for every short its first 20-day-high close.
rule_main.overlap: one position per market (kit.sim mode 'one'); every-signal variant (mode 'every') for the every-signal bar. Basket of the 14 markets, one rule, same parameters.

what_changed: No crypto (the brief's own decision of 2026-11-18): 14 markets.

The kit's event exit is per market, not per side; the side-dependent channel exit is expressed as the per-market event set of the breakout state machine above, which gives every long and every short trade exactly its own exit condition. The random-entry null re-enters on random days with the same per-market events (kit design): a random long entered while the market's state is short leaves at the first 20-day-HIGH close; the null is therefore the kit's same-exit null, not a side-specific channel null.

A reversal (a 50-day close breakout on the opposite side on the very close that exits the open trade) enters at the bar where the open trade exits; the kit's one-position rule requires the next entry to open AFTER the exit bar, so such a reversal is skipped (counted and reported). Later signals of that side enter normally.
Days with fewer than 5 hourly bars (one-bar holiday stubs) are not daily closes.
Daily close known at the 17:00 NY boundary even on early-close days (conservative).
costs: kit.costs (lab/r2/fp_costs.json, FP Raw): gross, net, spread and slippage x1.5; swaps every night (slow track).
bars: CHARTER.md 'The bars' for a basket on 01_main, computed by kit.judge.verdict(..., max_hold_tdays=40): t on daily sums >= 2.5, pooled PF >= 1.12 and >= 1.04 at costs x1.5, >= 60 % years positive, >= 65 % markets positive, no market above 25 % of the profit, neighbours' median PF >= 1.06, every-signal expectancy > 0, hold <= 40 trading days, same-day random-entry null >= 97.5 (2000 draws, the main's own exit, stop and events), weekly corr with the ten <= 0.30, truncation tests (signals and events) with default cuts; deflated Sharpe on N_all reported.
split: IS only (to 2021-12-31). No validation look in this run (the lead does it).
